original_question: For distinct positive integers h1, ..., hr with r >= 3 and integers k1, ..., kr >= 1, find a conjectural asymptotic formula for sum_{n<=x} d_{k1}(n+h1) d_{k2}(n+h2) ... d_{kr}(n+hr), analogous to the Hardy-Littlewood style conjectural asymptotic for sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n+h1) ... Lambda(n+hr).
target_in_paper: Section "Additive divisor sums/shifted convolution sums", Problem (28), page 11. This paper is a problem list rather than a theorem paper with labels like Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, and your draft clearly targets Problem (28). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17800))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's wording: it uses distinct positive shifts h1,...,hr, requires r >= 3, takes positive integer indices k1,...,kr, asks for a conjectural asymptotic for sum_{n<=x} d_{k1}(n+h1)d_{k2}(n+h2)...d_{kr}(n+hr), and explicitly frames the problem as analogous to the Hardy-Littlewood conjectural asymptotic for sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n+h1)...Lambda(n+hr). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the notation d_k(n) should be defined: for k > 0, zeta(s)^k = sum_{n>=1} d_k(n)/n^s. In this problem the paper then specializes to positive-integer tuples (k1,...,kr). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

The asymptotic variable should be stated explicitly: the conjectural formula is meant as x -> infinity. The paper leaves this implicit in the problem statement. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

For a sharp stand-alone formulation, r, the tuple (k1,...,kr), and the distinct shifts h1,...,hr should be treated as fixed parameters; the paper does not specify any uniformity range in the h_i, so one should not add one. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
If the Hardy-Littlewood comparison is retained, Lambda should be identified as the von Mangoldt function. This is a self-containedness issue rather than an extra hypothesis.

The paper asks only for a conjectural asymptotic formula; it does not ask for a proof, an explicitly stated error term, or a broader generalization beyond this r-fold shifted divisor-correlation problem. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
refined_question: Given fixed r >= 3, fixed positive integers k1,...,kr, and fixed distinct positive integers h1,...,hr, where d_k(n) is the k-th divisor function defined by zeta(s)^k = sum_{n>=1} d_k(n)/n^s, formulate, as x -> infinity, a conjectural asymptotic formula for sum_{n<=x} d_{k1}(n+h1)d_{k2}(n+h2)...d_{kr}(n+hr), in a form analogous to the Hardy-Littlewood conjectural asymptotic for sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n+h1)...Lambda(n+hr), where Lambda denotes the von Mangoldt function. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem (28) in the section "Additive divisor sums/shifted convolution sums". The introduction supplies only thematic context—namely that additive divisor sums are central in moment problems and that Conrey-Keating introduced new types of such sums—while the notation section supplies the essential definition of d_k. Problem (28) itself gives the precise scope: r-fold shifted divisor correlations with r >= 3, positive-integer indices (k1,...,kr), distinct positive shifts h1,...,hr, and an analogy with the Hardy-Littlewood prime-tuple asymptotic; it also notes that Ng-Thom and Tao derived conjectures only in the r = 2 case by probabilistic arguments. Because the paper does not impose a uniformity range or an error term here, adding those would go beyond the paper's stated intent. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
